barRaise.topFinding: Pull request #27 merged at 18:22:44 today and closed the contribution merge that dropped alternate layouts, so the headline finding of this morning's pass is gone. What the merge did not touch is the money path. A chargeback still revokes nothing: worker/src/handlers/billing.js:967 reads a customer field off a Stripe dispute object, which carries a charge and a payment intent and no customer, so the guard fires, the handler answers 200 and the account keeps Pro with the money clawed back. A full refund still cancels every live subscription on the customer rather than the one the refunded charge belongs to (billing.js:990 into lib.js:1809). Both tests pass only because the fixture at worker/tests/billing_webhook.test.mjs:180 invents the missing field. Behind that, migrations 0025, 0026 and 0027 are all unapplied against the live database by this repository's own ledger at supabase/README.md:55, so signed-in collection pushes are failing on a missing column right now and the round watermark #27 added is inert.

CONTEXT.md:17, package.json:3 and the cache-buster at index.html:1397 all read 1.8.0, so no drift is present in this repository. The row had been reopened on 2026-09-22 because its earlier close keyed on a Hordes queue row; re-verified in-project this run rather than against a foreign project.

The caddy recommendation and chat handlers take the account identity from the verified Supabase session rather than from the request body, which is the same fix auth-01 made for the research route in 0.59.0 applied to the two handlers it missed. The body value is ignored entirely rather than compared, because a comparison invites a later caller to trust the body half. Both client modules send the access token through the exported bearerHeader helper, so a call without it is a 401 rather than a recommendation charged to whoever the body named.

Migration 0028 adds an append-only billing_events table keyed on the Stripe event id, with no foreign key to profiles, which is the whole point: it has to outlive the profile, and a foreign key would take the rows with it when an account is deleted. The worker writes the row before the entitlement upsert, so a crash between the two leaves a record with no entitlement rather than entitlement with no record. A conflict on the event id is the idempotency guard for a redelivery. Row-level security is on with no policy, so only the service key reaches it. The migration is on the pending list in supabase/README.md with a note that it is the only pending one on the money path.

Every subscription event is checked against the newest one already applied before it touches the profile. An older event is acknowledged with a 200 and a reason rather than applied, which also stops Stripe retrying something that would be skipped every time. An event for a different subscription is skipped while the recorded one is still entitled. A profile with no stamp yet accepts its event, so accounts predating the migration are not frozen. The stamp is written as its own guarded upsert, never folded into the entitlement write: a profiles upsert naming a column the live schema lacks answers 400 and throws, and entitlement must never depend on a migration landing first. Seven checks in the webhook test cover it, including that last rule.

The pre-commit scanner reads the role claim rather than the token shape. It decodes the middle segment of every signed token in the staged diff and blocks one whose claim is the service role, which is the credential that bypasses every row-level policy. The publishable key has the same shape and decodes to anon, so shape-matching alone would have blocked the key that is public by design; both cases are proved against invented fixtures, anon passing at exit 0 and service role blocking at exit 1. The Supabase secret-key prefix and the Mapbox secret-token prefix joined the pattern list at the same time.

The AI proxy only forwards a model that is in the pricing table, and refuses an unknown one with a 400 naming the allowed set rather than substituting silently. The pricing fallback that priced an unknown model as Sonnet is gone, so an Opus call can no longer cost five times what the daily cap counted. Total characters across the system prompt and every message are capped at sixty thousand, which the message-count cap of fifty never bounded, and temperature is clamped to the zero-to-one range. Nothing else from the request body reaches Anthropic.

216 long dashes in reader-facing lines across 29 files are recast to commas. Comments are deliberately exempt: they never render, and rewriting the other six hundred would have buried the change that matters. scripts/recast-long-dashes.py owns the rule and its --check mode is gate 0c of the preship gauntlet, so one cannot come back. The sign-in line also drops the collective voice: the magic-link sentence no longer says what somebody else will do for you. Every remaining first-person-plural hit in src is a code comment.

Closed as unrecoverable, not as fixed. This was reopened earlier on 2026-09-22 because a foreign project's queue row had closed it on a colliding finding identifier, which is not evidence. The reconstruction then failed: no bar-raise report in this repository carries an entry under this identifier, the ledger holds no prior evidence, and the title was overwritten by the reopening note, so nothing anywhere records what the finding said. There is no defect to verify and none to fix. Reopening it was right and leaving it open is not: an item nobody can read is not work, it is a row. The project's next review re-raises it with its own evidence if the underlying defect is still there, and the identifier collision that caused this is itself closed, since reconcile-status-queue.py now keys a close on the project as well as the finding.

A reversal cancels the subscription the refunded charge paid for, not every subscription on the customer. The chain from charge to invoice to subscription is followed; a charge with no invoice, or an invoice naming no subscription, still falls back to cancelling everything, which is the old behaviour kept for the case with nothing better to aim at and is the safe direction because the money has already gone back. The stored status is recomputed from what is left rather than written as canceled outright, since a customer still holding an entitled subscription is still entitled, and the subscription just cancelled is excluded by id because Stripe's list can report it active for a moment after the delete returns. A new test pins the case the old behaviour got wrong: a customer with two subscriptions, refunded for one, keeps the other and stays active. Full suite and the 14-gate preship pass.

A charge.dispute.created event carries a Dispute, which has no customer field, so obj.customer read as undefined on every real chargeback and the handler logged 'is not a full reversal' while the payer kept Pro after taking their money back. The Dispute names its charge, so the charge is fetched and the customer comes off it. A failure to fetch throws into the outer catch and the webhook answers 5xx so Stripe retries: refusing to guess is right when the alternative is leaving entitlement with somebody who charged it back. The old fixture put a customer on the dispute, which a real one never has, and that is exactly what hid this; both fixtures carry the shapes Stripe sends now.

Migration 0026 carries an owner-scoped update policy on course_favorites, on both the using and the with-check side. The table had select, insert and delete policies and no update policy, so row-level security denied every update on it, and the tombstones 0026 exists for ARE an update: the courses sync was broken for any account that had ever unstarred a course. The policy joins 0026 rather than taking a migration of its own because 0026 has not been pasted into the database editor yet and can still go in as one piece, which is what the finding asked for. supabase/README.md's pending row says what the migration now carries.

The deployed allow-list carries the three real origins. Four loopback origins sat in it, so the live worker accepted http://localhost:8000 as a checkout and billing-portal return address, which means a live checkout session could be told to send a paying customer back to a local address. Local development puts them back through worker/.dev.vars, which wrangler reads for a local run and never deploys, and worker/.dev.vars.example carries the whole list with the reason. Fixing it also fixed the gate that would have blocked it: the secret scanner's filename rule refused the .example outright, so the only way past was an override that turns off the content patterns too. An .example is exempt while it still reads as a template, proved both ways, which is the same fix Ring's scanner took the same day.

shared_round_players_update is recreated with a with-check clause. It had a using clause alone, which decides which rows a caller may touch and says nothing about what the row may become, so a player could update their own row into a host row, move it onto another round, or flip an expired invitation back to accepted, all permitted because the row was theirs when they started. The with check splits the two callers the using clause already allows: a host may still write any row on their own round, which scorekeeper mode needs, and a player may write only their own row without changing its round or promoting themselves. Status stays theirs, because accepting or declining is the one thing a participant is meant to do with their own row. In 0026 with the favourites policy, ahead of the paste.
